requirements_summary: Dedicated (VPC) capacity. Primary KPIs: p95 < 800ms, p99 < 1500ms for chat during peak; embeddings batch jobs off-peak. Workload is bursty (end-of-month spikes; daily peaks 10am-2pm ET). They accept higher baseline capacity if it eliminates oscillation-induced latency. Need clear routing behavior during capacity constraints (no unexpected model/version changes) and fast confirmation signals for mitigations. Wants predictable scaling behavior: min replicas enforced, scale-down cooldowns, and guardrails against oscillation.
technical_notes: Observed pattern: autoscaler scales up rapidly, then scales down too aggressively; GPU pool churn correlates with queueing + tail latency spikes. Customer reports user-visible timeouts in their agent UI during churn windows. Current mitigations discussed: (1) set min replicas above steady-state baseline; (2) extend scale-down cooldown to reduce thrash; (3) cap scale-down rate; (4) pre-warm capacity before known peak windows. Customer asked for a "stability mode" toggle and/or Redwood-managed policy that prioritizes latency stability over cost during peak hours. They also asked whether burst capacity (SUP-1853) can be guaranteed to activate within a bounded window; they want an explicit escalation trigger if burst does not engage.
current_deployment: Dedicated GPU pool in us-east; planning second pool in eu-west for DR + regional latency. Using streaming chat for agent UX; embeddings for internal search indexing nightly. Monitoring via Redwood Console + their Datadog (exported metrics).
